facts.value: Treasury & Investment Strategies 2026/27 (updated Feb 2026) — 44-page pack. Covering report + Appendix 1 (Treasury Policy) + Appendix 2 (Treasury Management Strategy) + Appendix 2a (Treasury Limits / prudential indicators) + Appendix 2b (Treasury Investment Strategy) + Appendix 3/3a (non-treasury investments). Advisor: MUFG.

source.title: Treasury & Investment Strategies 2026/27 — Council, 25 February 2026, paper 169493

facts.note: Report author Chris Raymakers (chris.raymakers@leicester.gov.uk). Lead director Amy Oliver, Director of Finance — signed 21 November 2025 (take title verbatim). Route was OSC 2 Feb 2026 (paper 168889) then Full Council 25 Feb 2026. The prudential indicators for the Capital programme (borrowing/CFR walk, financing-cost ratio) are NOT in this pack — they sit with the 2026/27 Capital Programme report elsewhere on the same agenda (§1.2, §4.2, §4.3). Treasury balance sheet, limits and operational side ARE in this pack.

source.title: Treasury & Investment Strategies 2026/27 — Appendix 2a §10 (Liability Benchmark), penultimate paragraph

facts.note: Paper text verbatim: 'The total debt including PFI and finance leases is £255m whereas our capital finance requirement was £595m.' No dated year printed against the £595m — full CFR walk sits with the separate Capital Programme report, not on disk.

facts.value: £193m long-term debt (£174m PWLB + £19m Unitary Status debt managed by Leicestershire County Council)
facts.note: Unitary Status debt is pre-1997 County debt Leicester took a share of on becoming a unitary; managed by Leicestershire CC and charged back. NOT PWLB and NOT in our loan file. Report signed 21/11/2025 so 'currently' reads as late-2025 snapshot.

source.title: Treasury & Investment Strategies 2026/27 — Appendix 2a §10, penultimate paragraph

facts.note: Implies other long-term liabilities (PFI + IFRS 16 leases) of £255m − £193m = £62m. Not printed separately.

Balance-sheet identity: CFR £595m − external £193m − OLTL £62m (implied) = £340m internal. Consistent with §15 (App 2) narrative: 'This position has now shifted as reserves and cash balances have been reduced and the council has borrowed to fund the capital programme.'

facts.value: External debt walking from £174m (31/03/2025 actual) → £209m avg 2025/26 → £229m avg 2026/27 → £240m avg 2027/28 → £256m avg 2028/29 — averages, +£82m over four years off a £174m base.
facts.note: Note these are ESTIMATED AVERAGES not year-end positions. §41 Appendix 2: 'in practice, we are unlikely to repay any PWLB loans during the remainder of 2025/26 or in 2026/27' — direction is net drawdowns not repayments.

facts.value: £650m borrowing + £500m other liabilities = £1,150m total (statutory ceiling under LGA 2003)
Upper limits on the maturity structure of fixed-rate borrowing: Under 12m £50m; 12m-24m £100m; 24m-5y £150m; 5y-10y £200m; 10y-25y £250m; 25y+ £350m. Lower limit £0 all bands.
facts.note: 25+ year bucket at £350m against a Liability Benchmark peak of ~£440m by ~2029/30 (chart p.27) is a member-level statement of intent that most future borrowing can sit at 25+ years. §41 App 2 caveats this: new borrowing likely at 'the shorter end of the market' to even out the maturity profile.

facts.value: 1% change in interest rates = £1m impact = 0.22% of Net Revenue Budget in 2026/27 (0.20% in 2027/28; 0.18% in 2028/29). Implied Net Revenue Budget ≈ £455m.
facts.note: §11 App 2a: 'As our borrowings are mostly fixed, we do not anticipate any changes on our borrowing costs in the event of interest rate changes on our existing loans.' The £1m is on the stock — sensitivity on rolling new draws is materially larger.

facts.value: £60m of asset sales over next 3 years, cash receipts in 2026/27 reflected in the treasury strategy indicators
Total treasury investments expected to average ~£100m in 2025/26 and 2026/27 (down from a peak; balances fell to ~£50m at end of 2024/25 before recovering as borrowing-fund model shifted).
Bank Rate 3.75% at drafting; strategy expected 'a further rate cut early in 2026/27' (§27 App 2)
facts.note: §9: 'During 2025/26 interest rates have been cut to 4% with the Bank of England expected to make further cuts in early 2026 to stimulate further growth.' §27: three 25bp cuts in May/Aug/Dec 2025 to 3.75%, 'strong prospect of a further rate cut early in 2026/27'. Bank Rate today (2026-08-16) is still 3.75% — the further cut has not happened.

facts.value: PWLB HRA rate 0.4% cheaper than certainty rate. Paper text: 'extended until March 2026'.
facts.note: The paper's 'until March 2026' text is pre-Autumn-Budget-24 boilerplate (Budget 30 Oct 2024 extended the discount to March 2027). Do NOT surface this as a correction to the DoF — EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §7 forbids inviting correction, and our own understanding of the current HMT position would need re-verification before quoting.

facts.value: £4.33m held in commercial property funds against a £30m limit; no current intention to invest new funds. 'Performance has been disappointing since we invested in these funds in 2018, though the capital losses have been outweighed by the income received to date.'
facts.note: Small footnote against the treasury balance sheet — not a material email talking point but useful colour on the non-treasury investment stance.

facts.value: DOES NOT TIE — recorded here, left out of the email. Paper (§11 App 2): £174m PWLB at drafting late 2025. Our file (price_book.py 'LEICESTER CITY COUNCIL') at 2025-11-30: 4 loans totalling £68,102,513 at weighted 4.1858%; at 2026-02-25 (meeting date): 12 loans totalling £187,950,059 at 4.2258%; at 2026-08-16 (today): 16 loans totalling £241,865,781 at 4.2358%. At 2025-03-31: NO loans outstanding — our file appears to hold only loans drawn from April 2025 onwards, missing the historic long-dated tail referred to in §41 App 2 ('significant proportion ... with over 25 years to run which are historic').

source.title: PWLB borrower file (price_book) reconciled against paper §11 Appendix 2

facts.note: Per PIPELINE.md: a failed reconciliation is not a reason to skip the email and NOT a reason to say anything about our data disagreeing with theirs. The draft mentions the coverage gap once, as disclosure (per EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md 'disclose our own coverage gaps'), without inviting a correction.

facts.value: TIES on the numbers the paper prints. CFR £595m − External borrowing £193m − Other long-term liabilities £62m (implied from £255m total debt including PFI/leases − £193m long-term debt) = £340m internal borrowing. That is 57% of the CFR.

source.title: Treasury & Investment Strategies 2026/27 — Appendix 2 §11 and Appendix 2a §10

facts.note: The £62m OLTL line is derived by subtraction — the paper does not print PFI + leases separately. §4 of Appendix 2a confirms both categories sit in 'other forms of liability'.

facts.value: Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75% between the paper's drafting (Nov 2025) and today (16 Aug 2026, six months after the Council meeting). The 'further rate cut early in 2026/27' the strategy leaned on (§27 App 2) has not happened.

source.title: Own market observation vs Treasury & Investment Strategies §27

facts.note: PWLB Certainty rates 2026-08-14 PM (notice 314/26): 5y 5.34%; 10y 5.83%; 20y 6.38%; 50y 6.27%. Paper does not print PWLB levels at drafting, so a like-for-like bp move is not derivable. What is derivable is the direction — Bank Rate expected to fall and has not.

summary.text:
A council in the middle of a live transition from internal-funded to externally-funded. On the paper's own numbers, £340m of a £595m Capital Financing Requirement is currently carried by cash and reserves — total debt including PFI and finance leases is £255m (Appendix 2a §10), and long-term debt is £193m (Appendix 2 §11: £174m PWLB plus £19m Unitary Status debt managed by Leicestershire County Council). Paragraph 15 of Appendix 2 is candid about what has changed: the position that meant Leicester 'had not needed to borrow for several years' has shifted as reserves and cash balances have been drawn down.

The forecast externalises steadily. Appendix 2a §9 walks average external debt from £174m at 31/3/2025 to £256m by 2028/29, +£82m across four years off a £174m base. The Liability Benchmark chart on page 27 pushes further, with the gross loans requirement rising toward a plateau in the late 2020s well above today's £255m total debt.

Loan-book reconciliation does not hold — our PWLB file for Leicester appears to hold only loans drawn from April 2025 onwards, missing the historic long-dated tail Appendix 2 §41 describes ('significant proportion ... with over 25 years to run which are historic'). The draft discloses that gap once, without inviting a correction. The rate hook is a testable one from the paper itself: §27 Appendix 2 leans on 'a strong prospect of a further rate cut early in 2026/27' — six months into 2026/27 that cut has not happened, and Bank Rate is where it was at drafting (3.75%). Advisor is MUFG (§47 App 2).

status.note: Send address for Chris Raymakers (report author) is published on page 2 of the paper. Amy Oliver's email is not published — flag for follow-on if we find it. Anchored to a mid-year OSC treasury report expected autumn 2026 (per §4.4 TMP: six-monthly to OSC); no specific date published in this pack.

officer.subject: £340m of your CFR is currently funded from cash
officer.body:
Dear Chris,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a couple of thoughts on the Treasury & Investment Strategies pack that went to Council on 25 February. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The strategy is clearly laid out and paragraph 15 of Appendix 2 is unusually direct about the transition Leicester is going through — this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

The reading that stood out is the size of the internal borrowing behind the numbers at paragraph 10 of Appendix 2a. Total debt including PFI and finance leases sits at £255m against a capital finance requirement of £595m, so about £340m of the CFR is currently carried by cash and reserves. Paragraph 15 of Appendix 2 is candid about what has changed: the position that meant Leicester 'had not needed to borrow for several years' has shifted as reserves and cash balances have been drawn down. The forecast table at paragraph 9 of Appendix 2a walks external debt from £174m at 31 March 2025 to £256m average by 2028/29 — around £82m of net new borrowing over four years off a £174m base — and the liability benchmark chart within paragraph 10 pushes the gross loans requirement further out beyond that horizon.

The other line worth flagging is paragraph 27 of Appendix 2. When the strategy was written, Bank Rate had just been cut to 3.75% and the report notes 'a strong prospect of a further rate cut early in 2026/27.' Six months on from the Council meeting, Bank Rate is still 3.75% — unchanged since the 18 December 2025 cut, and no further cut has come in the first four and a half months of 2026/27. That is a testable position the paper takes, and the market has answered it in one direction. PWLB certainty rates on Friday's PM fixing sit at 5.34% at 5 years, 5.83% at 10 years and 6.38% at 20 — worth watching against paragraph 42's move to consider Equal Instalments of Principal alongside the historic maturity-basis approach as the next tranche is drawn.

Where you might find us most useful: we price every published council's PWLB book against the DMO's premature repayment curve daily at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. One caveat we owe you before you look: our PWLB file for Leicester currently holds loans drawn from April 2025 onwards, and appears to be missing the historic long-dated tail referred to in paragraph 41. We are flagging that rather than presenting our numbers as your position. Break costs there are indicative only and only the DMO can quote. What we can quote against the market with confidence is anything drawn during this strategy period, and the monthly sector totals at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — so a next-draw decision can be benchmarked against what the sector actually did that month, not what it did six months ago.

One standing point because CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates will put it in front of every S151: the liability benchmark pathway becomes central to how the whole strategy is framed. An interactive version tied to our rate feeds sits at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — for a council walking a large slice of internal borrowing toward external, being able to move the reserves path and see the crossover shift is the useful thing.

On training, four look most relevant to Leicester. Strategic PWLB borrowing is the closest match to the multi-year programme walking out in Appendix 2a. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice sits directly on the chart within paragraph 10. HRA treasury & self-financing picks up the concessionary rate the strategy leans on at paragraph 18. Interest rate risk covers the £1m sensitivity at paragraph 11 of Appendix 2a and the exposure that builds as new borrowing replaces internal. For members, The Capital Strategy for members is written for the Council seat that approved this pack. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts are available for the whole team.

And if any of it is useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury & Investment Strategies 2026/27 (updated Feb 2026), Full Council 25 February 2026, at https://cabinet.leicester.gov.uk/documents/s169493/treasury-management-strategy-report-updated-feb26.pdf
